gaps.sentence: The money was divided ___ the four children.
gaps.hint: for a group of more than two
gaps.explanation: 'Among' is traditionally used for more than two; 'between' is preferred for exactly two.

gaps.sentence: She has lived in this street ___ 2015.
gaps.hint: starting point of a period up to now
gaps.explanation: 'Since' is used with a point in time when the situation started and continues; 'for' is used with a length of time.

gaps.sentence: Pens, envelopes and paper are sold in the ___ department.
gaps.explanation: 'Stationery' means writing materials; 'stationary' is an adjective meaning not moving.

gaps.sentence: There was ___ anything left in the fridge.
gaps.hint: adverb meaning almost not at all
gaps.explanation: 'Hardly' means almost not ('hardly anything'); 'hard' means with effort or solid.
'Valuable' means worth a lot of money; 'valued' means appreciated; 'invaluable' already means priceless, so it is not graded.

gaps.hint: the uncountable activity of travelling in general
gaps.explanation: 'Travel' is uncountable when it means travelling in general; the other options are countable nouns.

gaps.sentence: She studied ___ for her final exams.
gaps.hint: adverb meaning with a lot of effort
gaps.explanation: 'Hard' is an adverb meaning with great effort ('work hard'); 'hardly' means almost not at all.
'Your' shows possession; 'you're' means 'you are'; 'yours' is a possessive pronoun standing alone.
